purpose: Structural rules of the 2005 collective bargaining agreement (effective 2005-06): contract lengths, raises, maximums, minimums, rookie scale, extensions, tax, escrow, exceptions, age limit. Live only from the agreement's ratification date; never applied to an earlier contract.
hindsight_warning: Everything here is real-world history. The 2005 CBA terms were not public until June 21, 2005 (agreement in principle) and not final until ratification on July 30, 2005; 2003-04 league averages are public only after the 2003-04 regular season closed (2004-04-14). Season-specific figures for 2006-07 onward printed in the source FAQ were deliberately NOT copied, to avoid future-season leakage; only structural rules and 2005-06 values are recorded.

status_legend.sourced: Read directly from the cited source.
status_legend.derived: Computed or inferred from sourced facts; reasoning given.
status_legend.unverified: Could not be confirmed from a primary or reliable source; value null or text marked as unconfirmed.

sources.title: Larry Coon, NBA Salary Cap FAQ (2005 CBA, final update), retrieved 2026-10-05
sources.note: Final update of the 2005-CBA FAQ (written up to 2011). Includes later-season figures and real 2005-11 transactions (hindsight).

agreement_in_principle.note: Announced by David Stern and Billy Hunter before Game 6 of the 2005 Finals; previous accord expired June 30, 2005. Also cbafaq05 Q6 ('late June 2005') and Q18 (amnesty eligibility keyed to players acquired before June 21, 2005).

ratified_and_signed.note: UPI dateline New York, July 30, 2005: the NBA and NBPA ratified and signed a new six-year agreement. cbafaq05 Q5: 'ratified ... in July 2005'.

nba_deal_points_release.note: Date of NBA.com 'CBA Principal Deal Points' as cited by Wikipedia; original page not fetched.

july_moratorium_2005.note: Extended in 2005 for the CBA to be finalized, ratified and distributed (Q6, Q93). UPI also gives Aug 2 as the day the new cap took effect.

value.league_option: 2011-12 (one-year extension at the league's option; not exercised)

term.note: UPI and AP both describe a six-year agreement. Whether the 2011-12 option was exercised is hindsight relative to 2005.

value: Players Association: certain types of collusion
League: significant drop in national TV revenue in the next TV agreement
Either side: certain CBA provisions struck down in court

salary_cap_2005_06.note: Agreed fixed figure; formula would have given about $50.9 million. Charlotte (expansion) $37.125 million. UPI also reports $49.5 million.

other_free_agents_max_years.note: Includes Early Bird, Non-Bird, Mid-Level and cap-room signings. 1999 CBA: 6.

sign_and_trade_min_years.note: Only the first season must be guaranteed.

rule.value: Raises are a percentage of the first-year salary (not compounded); decreases limited by the same amount. Raises take effect July 1.

rookie_scale_pct.note: Annual raises limited to 8% and may not exceed 120% of that season's scale amount.

definition.note: The cap used for maximums is computed at 48.04% of projected BRI, not the 49.5%/51% salary-cap percentage.

2005_06.note: Hard figures agreed for 2005-06 rather than the formula. Later seasons are in the FAQ but deliberately not copied.

105_pct_rule.value: A free agent's first-year maximum is never less than 105% of his salary in the last year of his previous contract, with any team.

applies_to.value: First season only; later seasons limited by raise rules.

years_of_service_credit.value: A season counts if the player is on an active or inactive list for at least one day of the regular season.

minimum_salary_2005_06.note: Keyed by years of service. The league reimburses salary above the 2-year minimum for 3+-year veterans on one-year minimum deals; only the 2-year minimum counts on team salary.

structure.value: Two guaranteed seasons plus team options for the third and fourth seasons.
structure.note: 1999 CBA (repo file): three seasons plus a team option for a fourth.

value.third_season_option: October 31 preceding the player's second season
value.fourth_season_option: October 31 preceding the player's third season
value.weekend_rule: next business day if October 31 is a weekend or holiday

option_year_raises.note: The FAQ's No. 1-pick table labels 26.1% as the 4th-year option raise over the 3rd-year salary and 30.0% as the qualifying-offer raise over the 4th; its prose calls them the 'third year' and 'fourth year' increases. The table labels are used; the No. 30 endpoints (80.5%, 50.0%) come from the prose.

full_scale_table.note: Full by-pick scale is in CBA Exhibit B (http://www.nbpa.org/sites/default/files/EXHIBIT B.pdf), not fetched.

unsigned_after_jan_10.value: Scale amount reduces daily from January 10 until signed.

rfa_after.value: Restricted free agent after the fourth season if both options exercised; unrestricted if either option declined.

rookie_trade_wait.value: A drafted rookie may be traded 30 days after signing (1999 CBA: three months after signing or December 15, whichever later).

required_tenders.purpose: Required Tenders and how long a club keeps a pick's exclusive rights, for the 2005 draft on (picks whose contracts belong to the 2005-06 league year and later, runtime/agreement.terms). Read by runtime/draft_rights.py.

applies_to.note: Agreement terms are keyed by the league year a contract belongs to (runtime/agreement.py); a 2005 pick signs for 2005-06, and Q43 keeps the 1999 scale rules only for players drafted before 2005. The 2005 draft and its tender deadlines (July 15, September 5) straddle ratification (July 30, 2005; dates.ratified_and_signed), but the deadlines are the same under both agreements (first_round, second_round below), so the choice moves no date.

tender_by.note: Q102 (dates referenced in the CBA): 'July 16: First round draft picks become free agents if not given a required tender', so the tender is due by July 15 after the draft, as under the 1999 agreement. Q102's pointer '(see question number 41)' is stale in the final update: Q41 is about compensation and Q42 (first-round picks) does not discuss the tender.

terms.value: a rookie scale contract (two seasons plus team options for the third and fourth, Q42) at 80% or more of the pick's scale
terms.note: The FAQ does not state the first-round tender's terms. The structure is the 2005 scale contract (Q42); the 80% floor is the 1999 rule (Art. X §3(a)), kept as a documented assumption. The check reads dates only.

window_from.note: The FAQ gives only the end of the window (September 5). The 1999 agreement's start (the two weeks before September 5, Art. X §3(b): August 22) is kept as a documented assumption.

tender_by.note: Q102: 'September 6: Second round draft picks become free agents if not given a required tender'.

terms.value: a one-year contract offer (at the minimum salary)
terms.note: Q93: 'A second round draft pick can accept a required tender, which is a one-year contract offer teams must submit to retain their rights to the player.' One year is sourced; the minimum salary is the 1999 rule (Art. I (vv)), kept as a documented assumption.

rights_until.value: the date of the next draft, unless the pick signs
rights_until.note: Q43: 'For all other players, the team retains the player's draft rights until the date of the next draft.' Unchanged from the 1999 agreement (1999 FAQ Q40).

value.non_nba_contract: a pick already under contract with, or signing with, a non-NBA team: the team keeps his rights until one year after that obligation ends
value.college: a pick who goes on to play college ball: until one year after the draft he would have entered had he not declared early; one eligible for college who does not play: until that draft

retained_beyond_next_draft.note: Not modelled (as under the 1999 agreement): a register entry that records one of these bases (draft_rights_retained) is checked against its own dated record (runtime/draft_rights.py).

rookie_scale_window.value: From the day after the July moratorium to October 31 preceding the player's last option season (provided the team picked up that option).

rookie_scale_length.value: Up to five seasons beyond the last option season (six total).

rookie_scale_first_year_salary.value: Any amount up to the player's maximum; raises up to 10.5% of the extension's first-year salary.

veteran_extension_deadline.value: Up to June 30, the day before the player would become a free agent.

veteran_extension_length.note: Five seasons total including seasons remaining on the current contract. FAQ Q47's summary table says 6 including remaining seasons; Q52 (detailed) and the NBA deal points as reported (wiki_cba search summary) say five total. Treat 5 as the rule; conflict flagged.

veteran_extension_salary.value: First extension year up to 110.5% of the last existing-contract salary (not above the player's free-agent maximum); raises up to 10.5% of the last existing-contract salary.

terms.source_ref: Q52; Q11 for the 105% free-agent maximum
terms.note: Numeric form of the sourced Q52 entries above, read by runtime/extensions.py. Q52: contracts under four seasons may not be extended; four- or five-season contracts (and six-season contracts signed on or after July 1, 2005) three years after signing, six- or seven-season contracts signed before July 1, 2005 four years after, an extended contract three years after the extension; a rookie-scale contract to October 31 before the last option season (option picked up), up to five seasons beyond it, the first year up to the player's maximum, raises up to 10.5% of the first extension year; any other extension to June 30, five seasons including those remaining (the current season counts as one), the first year up to 110.5% of the last salary and not above the player's free-agent maximum, raises up to 10.5% of the last salary. Q11: a free agent's first-year maximum is never less than 105% of his last salary. The October 31 weekend rule (next business day) is not modelled: the career decides on October 31, as runtime/options.py does.

option_clause.note: Q51: "An option clause allows a contract to be extended for one additional season after the date it is scheduled to end ... Team Options give the team the right to invoke the option. There can be only one option year (except in the case of rookie scale contracts). Player Options give the player the right to invoke the option. There can be only one option year." A contract may not hold two options in the same season. Read by runtime/extensions.py when Wade's own extension terms ask for an option season: one, the last season of the extension, inside the five additional seasons a rookie-scale extension allows (Q52).

rate.value: $1 per $1 of team salary above the tax level

level_basis.value: 61% of projected BRI, minus projected benefits, adjusted for prior-season BRI, divided by the number of non-expansion teams; set before the season.
level_basis.note: 1999 CBA: 61.1% of actual BRI, set after the season, triggered only when escrow fell short; cliff smoothing removed.

levied_every_season.note: Disconnected from escrow; 1999 tax applied only in seasons when escrow failed.

level_2005_06.note: Fixed figure; formula would have given about $63.7 million.

measured_on.value: Team salary on the date of the team's last regular-season game, with bonus/trade-bonus/grievance adjustments; non-draft free agents below the 2-year minimum are taxed at the 2-year minimum.

distribution.value: Escrow and tax money shared equally among teams (no cliff provision).

withholding_2005_06_pct.note: FAQ table: 10% in 2005-06, then 9%, falling to 8% later. A web-search summary of a later ESPN piece mentioned 8%; the FAQ season table is used.

shortfall.value: If escrow is insufficient, the remainder is deducted from players the following season.

mid_level.note: UPI also reports $5 million. 2004-05 under the 1999 CBA was $4.903 million (repo cap file).

value.frequency: not in consecutive seasons; if the $1 Million exception was used in 2004-05 the Bi-Annual is unavailable in 2005-06

value.max_salary: greater of 175% of previous salary or average salary ($5 million defined for 2005-06)
greatest of 120% of previous salary, 120% of minimum, or the qualifying-offer amount

value.proration: reduces daily from first day of season

disabled_player.value: Lesser of 50% of injured player's salary or average salary; league approval; up to 5 years; trade use limited to 100% + $100,000.

january_10_proration.value: From January 10, unused Mid-Level, Bi-Annual, Larry Bird, Early Bird and Non-Bird exceptions reduce daily (new in 2005).

traded_player_salary_matching.value: Over-cap team may take back 125% + $100,000 of outgoing salary (1999 CBA: 115% + $100,000).

qualifying_offer.value: 125% of previous salary or minimum salary + $175,000, whichever is greater (rookie-scale QOs by draft position); one season; due June 30; must be accepted by March 1; withdrawable without consent until July 23.

arenas_provision.value: Offer sheets to RFAs with one or two years of service are limited to the average salary in year 1, 8% raise in year 2, then year 3 may jump to what the unrestricted amount would have been; later raises limited to 6.9% of year 3.

rule.value: U.S. players: at least 19 during the calendar year of the draft and one year removed from high-school graduation (class). International players: at least 19 during the calendar year of the draft.
rule.note: 1999 CBA: 18 and high-school class graduated. Also AP June 21, 2005 and The Draft Review ('increase from 18 to 19, plus one year removed from high school').

first_draft_affected.note: The rule did not affect players drafted before the CBA took effect (FAQ: Andrew Bynum, 17 when drafted in 2005, was eligible). The 2005 draft (June 28, 2005) preceded ratification (July 30, 2005), so the 2006 draft was the first held under it. No primary source with the explicit sentence '2006 draft' was fetched.

value.who: Only the player's own free agent (Bird, Early Bird or Non-Bird, even if renounced); not via Mid-Level, Bi-Annual or Disabled Player exceptions
value.guarantee: only first season must be guaranteed
value.atomic: contract void unless traded to the named team within 48 hours
value.byc: signed player may become a Base Year Compensation player
value.trade_bonus: not earned on the sign-and-trade itself
value.signing_bonus: either team may pay; signing team's share counts toward the $3 million trade cash limit

value.eligible: players signed or acquired before 2005-06-21, or already waived when the CBA took effect
value.effect: player's salary excluded from luxury-tax computation only; still paid and still counts on the cap; team may not re-sign or reacquire him for the length of the terminated contract

amnesty_2005.note: Real usage list (incl. Miami waiving Wesley Person) is in the FAQ; it is hindsight about real clubs and not copied here.

trades_and_consent.value: A player on a one-year contract who will have Bird or Early Bird rights cannot be traded without his consent; if he consents he becomes a Non-Bird free agent (1999: could not be traded). Base Year Compensation expires after six months or June 30, whichever later.

value.rule: A player playing under a one-year contract (excluding any option year) who will have Larry Bird or Early Bird rights at the end of it cannot be traded without his consent.
value.covers: Includes a first-round pick who, after his fourth (option) season, accepts his club's qualifying offer for his fifth season.
value.option_year: When an option year is involved the club can get around the rule by invoking the option before the trade (the contract is then no longer a one-year contract).
value.consent_effect: If he consents and is traded he loses his Larry Bird or Early Bird rights and enters free agency as a Non-Bird free agent: the club loses its Larry Bird or Early Bird rights.
value.timing_example: Seattle signed Vladimir Radmanovic to a one-year qualifying offer on September 21, 2005: he could not be traded at all until December 21, 2005 (the newly signed restriction, three months or December 15, whichever later), and after that only with his consent.

bird_clock.counts: seasons with the same club without being waived or changing teams as a free agent: a single contract or any series of contracts; a partial season counts as a full season
bird_clock.trade: a traded player's new club inherits his Bird rights (a trade does not reset the clock)
bird_clock.resets: changing teams by signing as a free agent; being claimed off waivers before clearing them; being selected in an expansion draft
bird_clock.waived: the player must complete his contract immediately before free agency (he cannot have been waived)
bird_clock.ten_day_contracts: do not count toward Bird rights
bird_clock.renounced: a club that renounces a player cannot use the Bird exception to re-sign him for one year; if he re-signs with his prior club (with cap room or the minimum) the renouncement ends with that contract and he is a Larry Bird free agent again at its end (Q34), so his return to that club does not reset the clock
bird_clock.re_signing: the clock resets only when he changes teams by signing as a free agent: a re-signing with the club holding his rights, in the summer or during the season, continues it; a player traded away, waived by his new club and re-signed by his old one changed teams as a free agent, so his clock resets (the FAQ's later example, not named here: it postdates the career clock)

exception_limits.early_bird: the greater of 175% of his previous salary or the average salary ($5 million defined for 2005-06)
exception_limits.non_bird: the greatest of 120% of his previous salary, 120% of the minimum salary, or the qualifying-offer amount

value.agreement_1999: Under the 1999 agreement such a player could not be traded at all (no consent route).

trade_consent_one_year_contract.source_ref: Q83 (one-year contract with Bird or Early Bird rights at its end, consent, Non-Bird free agency, the Radmanovic timing), Q88 (excluding any option year; the fifth-season qualifying offer; invoking the option before the trade; the newly signed restriction), Q26 (the Bird clock), Q34 (a renounced player re-signed by his prior club), Q19 (Early Bird and Non-Bird limits), Q37 and Q40 (the qualifying offer; restricted again with three or fewer seasons), Appendix (the 1999 difference)
trade_consent_one_year_contract.note: Read by runtime/trades.py (ConsentBook, consent_chance) for trades decided on or after CONSENT_FROM, 2005-11-01; every earlier trade replays unchanged. The rule existed in a stricter form under the 1999 agreement; it is not applied to the 2003-04 and 2004-05 trades already recorded.

over_36_rule.value: Contracts for players reaching age 36 may be classified Over-36: late seasons become 'zero years' whose salary is treated as deferred and charged against earlier cap years. Applies to contracts signed on or after November 1, 2005; contracts signed before that used the 1999 CBA rule.

value.inactive_list: players beyond 12 active; at least one inactive; set game by game; no minimum stay (replaces Injured Reserve with its 5-game minimum)
value.d_league: up to two players with fewer than two years of service may be assigned
value.ten_day_limit: no more 10-day contracts than players on the inactive list

roster.note: Max-three inactive also cited by Wikipedia from NBA.com Aug 4, 2005 deal points.

summary.value: Enforcement against hand-checking was tightened for 2004-05: defenders could no longer use hands or forearms on the perimeter to impede a ball handler, removing most perimeter contact and hand fighting.
summary.note: SI (Nadkarni, 2022): "In '04, the league did away with hand checking, removing most contact and hand fighting on the perimeter, giving offensive players much more breathing room to operate."

exact_rule_text_and_approval_date.note: Could not retrieve the 2004-05 Official Rules (Rule 12B) text or a dated NBA.com/Board of Governors/Competition Committee release. Secondary web summaries say the crackdown applied above the free-throw line extended and came with clarified block/charge calls and stricter defensive three-seconds enforcement; these are unconfirmed and not dated.

related_emphasis.value: Clarified blocking fouls and stricter calling of defensive three seconds as part of the same package.

defensive_three_seconds.value: Not new in 2004-05: introduced for 2001-02 together with legalized zone defense (Board of Governors vote April 12, 2001); backcourt count also cut from 10 to 8 seconds in 2001-02. A violation is a team technical: one free throw and the offense keeps the ball.
defensive_three_seconds.note: Corroborated by sr_rules for the 2001-02 entry. Any 2004-05 change was enforcement emphasis only (unverified).

league_expansion_30_teams.value: Charlotte Bobcats began play in 2004-05, making 30 teams.

realignment.value: Six divisions of five teams (three per conference); New Orleans Hornets moved from East to West; approved by the NBA (NBA.com release Nov 17, 2003). Schedule: 16 division games (4 x 4), 36 other in-conference games (4 vs six teams, 3 vs four, rotating), 30 vs the other conference (2 each).
realignment.note: Inter-conference count derived: 82 - 16 - 24 - 12 = 30, i.e. 2 vs each of 15 teams.

playoff_seeding.note: 2004-05 seeding (three division winners seeded 1-3) not confirmed here.

inactive_list_replaces_injured_list.value: From 2005-06 the active and inactive lists are set game by game, one hour before tip-off, with no minimum stay; replaces the Injured List (5-game minimum).
inactive_list_replaces_injured_list.note: Wikipedia quotes NBA.com 'Inactive vs. Active List Rules', Nov 1, 2005; also cbafaq05 Appendix.

dress_code.value: League dress code announced October 17, 2005, effective from the start of 2005-06 (off-court conduct rule, not a playing rule).

playing_rule_changes.note: No 2005-06 on-court playing-rule change could be confirmed from a reliable source.
